metaDescription: Atelier North designs homes, workplaces and cultural buildings. See featured projects and start a conversation about yours.

hero.title: Buildings that
hero.sub: We design homes, workplaces and cultural buildings that fit their street, their climate and the people who use them every day.
hero.proof: Our drawings are buildable. Every line is checked against structure, light and cost before it leaves the studio.
hero.alt: Blueprint style line drawing of a house with a grid background

benefits.title: Design that survives contact with reality

items.title: Drawn to be built
items.body: Structure, services and cost are worked through in the drawing, not discovered on site.

items.title: Designed for the climate
items.body: Shade, breeze and sun are planned first, so rooms stay cool without working hard.

items.title: Built with the client
items.body: You see the model at each stage and change it while change is still cheap.

items.title: On site until the end
items.body: We visit the site through construction and check the work against the drawings.

tagline: A good building is quiet. It gives you shade at noon, light in the morning, and a room that feels right before you know why.

how.title: From first sketch to finished building

steps.title: Listen and measure
steps.body: We walk the site with you, study the light and the rules, and agree the brief in writing.

steps.title: Design in stages
steps.body: Concept, then developed design, then construction drawings, each shown to you before we move on.

steps.title: Build and check
steps.body: We help you choose a builder, then visit the site and check the work as it rises.

collection.title: Work from the studio
collection.sub: Sample projects. Figures shown are demo figures for this page.
collection.emptyBody: Try a different word or clear the filters to see every project.

items.title: Courtyard house, Zamalek
items.desc: A family house arranged around a shaded courtyard, with bedrooms that catch the morning breeze.

items.title: Riverside studio offices
items.desc: Two floors of open studios above a shared ground floor, with deep balconies against the afternoon sun.

items.title: The small library
items.desc: A neighbourhood library with one long reading room, a garden court and a roof that shades the street.

items.title: Desert edge house
items.desc: A low house on the desert edge, with thick walls, small west windows and a courtyard open to the sky.

items.title: Workshop and showroom
items.desc: A furniture workshop with a street showroom, where making and selling share one honest space.

items.title: Gallery in the old town
items.desc: A careful conversion of a 1920s hall into a gallery, keeping the old walls and adding light from above.

people.title: A small studio, on site often
people.sub: Architects, an engineer and a model maker, working on a few projects at a time.

items.name: Layla Hassan
items.body: Layla leads design and has drawn houses and public buildings across Egypt for fifteen years.

items.name: Omar Sabry
items.body: Omar leads workplace projects and the studio model making, where ideas are tested by hand.

items.name: Mona Adel
items.body: Mona runs site visits and keeps drawings, builders and budgets in agreement.

items.name: Hatem Nour
items.body: Hatem checks every structure before it is drawn for construction.

proof.title: Clients who live and work in our buildings

items.quote: The house is cool at noon without air conditioning. The shade was drawn into the plan, not added later.
items.name: Dina El Ashry

items.quote: We saw a model at every stage. By the time we built, there were no surprises left.
items.name: Karim El Tayeb

items.quote: They visited the site every week and caught mistakes before they became expensive.
items.name: Sara Mokhtar

pricing.title: How design fees are arranged
pricing.sub: Fees depend on the size and stage of the project. They are agreed in writing before design starts.
pricing.note: All figures are confirmed in writing before work starts. An introductory meeting is free.

faq.title: Questions clients ask before we start

items.q: How long does a house design take?
items.a: A typical house takes three to five months from brief to construction drawings, depending on size and approvals.
Yes. We prepare the permit drawings and follow the file, but the decision and timing sit with the authority.

items.q: Can you work with our builder?
items.a: Yes. We work with the builder you choose, or introduce builders we have worked with before.

items.q: What do you need from us to start?
items.a: The site papers, a survey if you have one, and a conversation about how you live and what the budget allows.
Fees depend on the project size and the stages you choose. They are agreed in writing before design starts.
We design the fixed interiors of our buildings, such as kitchens and joinery, and we work with interior designers for loose furniture.

form.title: Tell us about your building

finalCta.title: Have a site and an idea?
finalCta.sub: Bring both to the studio. We will draw the first sketch together and tell you honestly what it will take.

footer.about: Atelier North is a Cairo architecture studio designing houses, workplaces and cultural buildings.
footer.privacyBody: We use the details you share only to answer your note. We do not sell your details. You can ask us to delete them at any time.
footer.termsBody: Projects on this page are samples for demonstration. Fees and timelines are confirmed in writing before any work starts.
